summary:
André Jobin (1786–1853) was a Montreal notary and politician who supported French-Canadian reform in Lower Canada and the Province of Canada. His political career spanned the Patriote movement, the aftermath of the 1837–38 rebellion, and the establishment of responsible government.

A prominent supporter of Louis-Joseph Papineau, Jobin served in the Lower Canada Assembly from 1835 until the constitution was suspended after the rebellion. He helped organize Patriote opposition, went into hiding, and was arrested in 1838 on a charge of sedition. He was released without trial.

Jobin later represented Montreal County in the Province of Canada Assembly. He supported Louis-Hippolyte LaFontaine, responsible government, and compensation for losses suffered during the rebellion. As a notary, he also secured reforms to the profession’s regulation and record-keeping. He helped found Montreal’s French-Canadian savings bank and served as the first president of the Montreal Board of Notaries. He retired from politics in 1851 and died in Sainte-Geneviève in 1853.
